# mmb-irb/mddb-workflow (commit 4e6dceeee67ce83650eed4aa2cfffe10107e2564)
# mmb-irb/mddb-workflow Overview
The [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) package orchestrates the lifecycle of Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulation projects. It converts raw simulation outputs into normalized files, executes automated Quality Assurance (QA) and analysis pipelines, and packages results with associated metadata. This system facilitates the standardization, validation, and analysis of MD simulation projects.

The package's core manages individual MD simulations and collections of simulations using [`MD`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L99) and [`Project`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L1333) classes. These classes integrate with a [`Task`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/tasks.py#L24) system for orchestrating input processing, remote data access, and lazy computation. See [Core Workflow Management and Data Lifecycle](#md-simulation-data-lifecycle-and-analysis-core-workflow-management-and-data-lifecycle) for more details.

A command-line interface (CLI) provides entry points for user interaction with the workflow. The CLI, defined in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/__main__.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/__main__.py) and [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py), offers subcommands for executing the main workflow, setting up inputs, performing data conversions, filtering, and managing datasets. Further information is available in [Command-Line Interface and Entry Points](#md-simulation-data-lifecycle-and-analysis-command-line-interface-and-entry-points).

Data management involves an SQLite database that tracks the status of projects and MD simulations. A distributed filesystem locking mechanism ensures data integrity, and Pydantic schemas validate complex input configurations. [Project and MD Dataset Management](#project-and-md-dataset-management) describes these mechanisms.

The workflow includes a suite of tools for various biophysical and structural calculations. These analyses encompass area per lipid, channel analysis, clustering, density profiling, dihedral energies, and principal component analysis. [Comprehensive MD Analysis Suite](#md-simulation-data-lifecycle-and-analysis-comprehensive-md-analysis-suite) provides an overview of these capabilities.

General-purpose utilities underpin the workflow's operations. These include persistent caching, file and path management, robust error handling, and reproducible argument checksums. The workflow integrates with external tools such as GROMACS, MDAnalysis, and Pytraj through specialized wrappers. Refer to [Workflow Utilities and Data Processing](#workflow-utilities-and-data-processing) for more information.

The workflow is containerized using Docker to ensure consistent execution across different environments. A Docker image encapsulates the Miniconda3 environment, dependencies, and the software itself. [Containerized Workflow Execution](#containerized-workflow-execution) details this setup.

## MD Simulation Data Lifecycle and Analysis
The [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) package manages the lifecycle of Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulation projects, from initial setup to data analysis and reporting. It orchestrates the standardization, validation, and analysis of MD simulation projects by converting raw simulation outputs into normalized files, performing automated Quality Assurance (QA) and analysis pipelines, and packaging results and metadata.

The workflow's command-line interface (CLI) is defined by [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/__main__.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/__main__.py) and [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py). This CLI provides various subcommands, enabling users to execute the main workflow, set up input files, convert data formats, filter and subset trajectories, modify structural chains, run Nucleic Acid Structural Statistical Analysis (NASSA), manage datasets, and update references. The [`main`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py#L199) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/__main__.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/__main__.py) serves as the primary entry point for executing the package as a script.

Core workflow management is handled by the [`MD`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L99) and [`Project`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L1333) classes, detailed in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py). The [`MD`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L99) class represents a single MD simulation, managing its input files, handling remote data retrieval, and integrating various analyses as [`Task`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/tasks.py#L24) instances. The [`Project`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L1333) class manages collections of [`MD`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L99) instances, overseeing project-level configurations and input management. Both classes employ lazy loading for properties and integrate remote data downloading capabilities.

Data management and input validation are central to the workflow, implemented in the [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core) directory. This includes tracking project and MD status in an SQLite database, ensuring data integrity with distributed filesystem locking, and generating configurations. Input validation is performed using Pydantic schemas, which ensure that input configurations are well-formed and consistent. For a detailed discussion of data management, refer to [Project and MD Dataset Management](#project-and-md-dataset-management).

The workflow offers a comprehensive suite of MD analysis tools, found in the [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses) directory. This suite covers diverse calculations such as area per lipid, channel analysis, clustering, density profiling, dihedral energies, interaction energies, helical parameters, hydrogen bonds, lipid interactions, and principal component analysis. These analyses often leverage external tools and libraries, with results consistently saved in JSON format.

General utilities and external tool integration, located in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils), underpin the workflow. These utilities include persistent caching mechanisms for performance optimization, robust file and path management, error handling, reproducible argument checksums, and managed interactions with remote MDDB servers. The workflow also provides seamless integration with external tools and libraries such as GROMACS, MDAnalysis, and Pytraj through specialized wrappers. For more information, see [Workflow Utilities and Data Processing](#workflow-utilities-and-data-processing).

The [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) is designed for consistent and reproducible execution across different environments through containerization using Docker, as described in [Containerized Workflow Execution](#containerized-workflow-execution). The [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile) encapsulates the Miniconda3 environment, dependencies, and the software itself, ensuring portability. Installation details, including for High-Performance Computing (HPC) environments, are outlined in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md).

### Core Workflow Management and Data Lifecycle
The MDDB workflow's central package, located at [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow), orchestrates the complete lifecycle of Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulation projects. This orchestration is managed primarily through two core classes, [`MD`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L99) and [`Project`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L1333), which integrate with a [`Task`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/tasks.py#L24) system to handle input processing, remote data access, and efficient, lazy computation.

The [`MD`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L99) class represents a single MD simulation, encapsulating all data and functionalities pertinent to it. This includes managing input files, whether they are local paths or remote URLs, and providing access to derived properties such as [`structure`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/structures.py#L1197), [`universe`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L880), and various atom [`Selection`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/selections.py#L6) objects. The [`MD`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L99) class is also responsible for integrating numerous analytical functionalities, which are often wrapped as [`Task`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/tasks.py#L24) instances for trackable and cacheable execution.

The [`Project`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L1333) class is designed to manage a collection of these [`MD`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L99) instances. It handles project-level configurations, such as input parameters, and can reference a specific "reference MD" for broader project operations. A key aspect of both [`MD`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L99) and [`Project`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L1333) classes is their use of lazy loading and computation for properties. This design ensures that complex calculations are performed only when their results are explicitly required, optimizing performance. They also incorporate robust mechanisms for downloading missing input files from a remote database if an [`accession`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs_schema.py#L139) is provided, promoting reproducibility and simplifying data access. Input validation and precedence rules are applied rigorously to parameters sourced from command-line arguments and configuration files, ensuring data integrity.

The integration with the [`Task`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/tasks.py#L24) system, defined in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/tasks.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/tasks.py), is fundamental to the workflow's efficiency. This system allows functions to be wrapped, enabling caching of results, trackable execution, and intelligent skipping of computations if outputs are already available. This modular approach, combined with extensive use of utility modules from [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils) and [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools), forms a highly organized and efficient framework for managing and analyzing MD simulation data. Further details on how project and MD data are managed, persisted, and validated can be found in [Project and MD Dataset Management](#project-and-md-dataset-management). The command-line interfaces for initiating and controlling these workflows are described in [Command-Line Interface and Entry Points](#md-simulation-data-lifecycle-and-analysis-command-line-interface-and-entry-points).

### Command-Line Interface and Entry Points
The MDDB workflow provides command-line interfaces (CLIs) as primary entry points for users to interact with and orchestrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulation projects. These CLIs are defined in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/__main__.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/__main__.py) and [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py), allowing the package to be executed directly from the terminal.

The main CLI functionality is implemented within [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py), which leverages Python's [`argparse`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py#L4) module to define a suite of subcommands. This subcommand-based structure organizes the workflow's diverse capabilities, making them accessible and manageable. A custom argument parser ([`CustomArgumentParser`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py#L106)) and formatter ([`CustomHelpFormatter`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py#L31)) enhance the user experience by providing improved help messages and specific error handling for subcommands. Help text for many arguments is dynamically generated from function docstrings, ensuring consistency between internal documentation and CLI usage.

The available subcommands facilitate various stages of the MD simulation data lifecycle:

*   **[`run`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/nassa_base.py#L109)**: This is the core command for executing the main MDDB workflow. It accepts numerous arguments to specify input files (topology, structure, trajectory), project configuration (directory, accession), and workflow control parameters (download behavior, setup, error handling, selection criteria, and task management).
*   **[`inputs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/inputs_generator.py#L12)**: Assists users in setting up and managing workflow input files, typically [`inputs.yaml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/conftest.py#L90). It can copy template files and optionally open them with a specified editor.
*   **[`convert`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/conversions.py#L34)**: Enables the conversion of molecular structures and trajectories between different file formats. It also supports merging multiple input trajectories into a single output.
*   **[`filter`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/structures.py#L2296)**: Allows users to apply atomic filtering to structures and/or trajectories based on a defined selection string and syntax. This is useful for removing unwanted elements or focusing on specific parts of a system.
*   **[`subset`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/DEVELOPMENT.md#L57)**: Extracts a subset of frames from a trajectory, providing options to specify start, end, and step values, or individual frames, which is useful for reducing trajectory size or isolating specific time points.
*   **[`chainer`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/structures.py#L2373)**: Modifies chain identifiers within PDB structures, often used for re-labeling or consolidating chains based on atom selections.
*   **[`nassa`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/conftest.py#L67)**: Manages and executes Nucleic Acid Structural Statistical Analysis (NASSA) pipelines. Users can generate configuration files, select specific analyses to run, and define input parameters for nucleic acid-specific computations, such as helical parameters.
*   **[`dataset`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L154)** (aliased as [`ds`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py#L349)): Provides comprehensive management for MDDB project datasets. This includes subcommands to add or remove projects, display their status, show a summary or live view of the dataset, generate [`inputs.yaml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/conftest.py#L90) files for projects, launch workflow execution for selected projects, and scan directories for new projects. This subcommand leverages the [Project and MD Dataset Persistence and Status Tracking](#project-and-md-dataset-management-project-and-md-dataset-persistence-and-status-tracking) for its operations.
*   **[`upref`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py#L548)**: Used for updating reference data across specified nodes and for various reference types, streamlining the maintenance of external data dependencies.

These command-line tools provide a structured and efficient way to interact with the MDDB workflow, enabling users to manage projects, run analyses, and process data without direct interaction with the underlying Python code.

### Data Management and Input Validation
Project and MD (Molecular Dynamics) simulation data are managed and validated through a centralized system that orchestrates the entire lifecycle. This system uses an SQLite database to maintain metadata about projects and their MD replicas, tracking their status and managing their execution. The core logic for this management resides primarily within the [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core) directory.

A key component for ensuring data integrity, especially in distributed computing environments, is the robust locking mechanism. The [`DatabaseLock`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L42) class, defined in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py), provides a distributed filesystem-safe lock. This mechanism uses directory creation to prevent race conditions when multiple processes attempt to access or modify the shared SQLite database simultaneously, a common challenge on network file systems where traditional file locks might be unreliable. The [`Dataset`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L154) class, also in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py), is responsible for interactions with this database, including adding new projects and MDs, updating their operational status (e.g., [`NEW`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L35), [`RUNNING`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L37), [`ERROR`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L38), [`DONE`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L39)), and retrieving comprehensive project information. This class also incorporates logic to automatically refresh the status of running jobs by checking their process IDs or SLURM job statuses, ensuring the database accurately reflects the current state of ongoing simulations. Furthermore, it enables the generation of [`inputs.yaml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/conftest.py#L90) files, critical for initializing and configuring individual simulation runs, often leveraging Jinja2 templates for flexibility.

Beyond data persistence and status tracking, the system places significant emphasis on validating and resolving complex input configurations. This is handled by the [`ProjectInputs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py#L36) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py) in conjunction with Pydantic schemas defined in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs_schema.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs_schema.py). These schemas rigorously define the expected structure and data types for workflow input files (e.g., [`inputs.yaml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/conftest.py#L90) or [`inputs.json`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/constants.py#L67)), covering aspects from project metadata to specific simulation and analysis parameters. The [`ProjectInputs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py#L36) class manages the loading, merging, and validation of these inputs from various sources, including file-based configurations and command-line overrides. It establishes a clear precedence for input values, ensuring that defaults are applied correctly and that any inconsistencies are flagged early through an [`InputError`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/auxiliar.py#L45). This system also includes specialized logic for merging and validating MD-specific configurations, supporting glob patterns for flexible file path specification, and ensuring the uniqueness and completeness of each MD setup. See [Advanced Input Configuration Resolution and Validation](#project-and-md-dataset-management-advanced-input-configuration-resolution-and-validation) for further details.

### Comprehensive MD Analysis Suite
The [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) repository provides a suite of tools for in-depth analysis of molecular dynamics (MD) simulation data, encompassing a wide range of biophysical and structural calculations. This analytical framework is primarily contained within the [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses) directory. It supports the characterization of membrane properties, conformational changes, and intermolecular interactions.

For analyzing membrane systems, the workflow can compute the Area Per Lipid (APL) using external tools to determine the surface area occupied by each lipid molecule. This process also grids the APL data and generates contour plots to visualize the distribution across the membrane. Channel analysis, particularly for protein pores, is performed using specialized external software to identify and characterize channels, including parsing pore-lining and pore-facing residues from its output. Lipid order parameters (S) are also calculated for all-atom, united-atom, and coarse-grained simulations, providing insights into membrane fluidity and lipid acyl chain orientation. Further details can be found in [Specialized Biophysical Analyses](#molecular-dynamics-analysis-tools-specialized-biophysical-analyses).

Conformational dynamics are explored through various methods. Clustering algorithms group similar conformations together based on RMSD, identifying representative frames and analyzing transitions between clusters. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is applied to trajectories to identify the dominant modes of motion, and can also be used to analyze changes in inter-residue contacts. Additionally, tools are available to generate data suitable for Markov State Models (MSM), which describe the kinetics and thermodynamics of conformational transitions. See [Conformational Sampling and Dynamics Analyses](#molecular-dynamics-analysis-tools-conformational-sampling-and-dynamics-analyses) for more information.

Interaction analyses quantify the energetic and structural relationships between different molecular components. This includes the calculation of dihedral energies (torsion, electrostatic, and Van der Waals) for specific rotatable bonds, providing insights into local flexibility and stability. Inter-residue distances are analyzed to map interaction networks, and hydrogen bond analysis identifies and quantifies these critical interactions. Furthermore, interaction energies between agents (e.g., protein-ligand, protein-protein) are computed using specialized tools that handle electrostatic and Van der Waals contributions. Lipid-protein interactions are specifically analyzed to classify contacts by lipid type and their head/tail parts. More detailed information can be found in [Intermolecular and Intramolecular Interaction Analyses](#molecular-dynamics-analysis-tools-intermolecular-and-intramolecular-interaction-analyses).

The suite also includes analyses for structural integrity and pocket detection. RMSD checks help verify the stability of trajectories by identifying sudden jumps that might indicate simulation artifacts. Tools for detecting and characterizing protein pockets, including their volume and implicated atoms, contribute to understanding potential binding sites. Consult [Structural Integrity and Pocket Detection](#molecular-dynamics-analysis-tools-structural-integrity-and-pocket-detection) for further reading.

Overall, the analytical tools leverage several external libraries such as [`mdtraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L22), [`pytraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L10), and [`MDAnalysis`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L877) for core molecular manipulation, alongside specialized third-party applications for specific calculations. The results are consistently saved in JSON format for easy integration with downstream analysis and visualization workflows.

### General Utilities and External Tool Integration
The [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) relies on a collection of general-purpose utilities that manage persistent data, handle file system operations, implement robust error management, and integrate with external molecular dynamics tools.

A persistent caching mechanism is provided by the [`Cache`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/cache.py#L8) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/cache.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/cache.py). This system stores and retrieves data from a designated file, designed to prevent redundant computations and ensure data consistency across multiple runs or concurrent processes. The cache is updated and saved atomically to safeguard against corruption. Functions can be wrapped using [`get_cached_function`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/cache.py#L79) to automatically cache their results based on input checksums.

File and path management are centralized within the [`File`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/file.py#L17) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/file.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/file.py). This class normalizes file paths, extracts metadata such as filename, extension, and format, and provides methods for file system operations. These operations include checksum generation, existence checks, symbolic linking, copying, and renaming. The class also handles format identification and provides compatibility checks for external tools like Pytraj.

The workflow integrates various external tools for molecular dynamics simulations. [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py) offers a standardized interface for executing GROMACS commands, managing environment variables, addressing mass definition issues, and parsing output logs for error reporting. This module includes utilities for extracting structures and trajectories, merging and converting trajectory files, and filtering atoms based on selections. Similarly, [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/mda_spells.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/mda_spells.py) facilitates the creation and manipulation of [`MDAnalysis`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L877) [`Universe`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L877) and [`Topology`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/topologies.py#L21) objects, focusing on handling molecular topology data, especially for lipids, including bond information and identification of acyl chains and head/tail groups. For Pytraj, [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/pyt_spells.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/pyt_spells.py) provides utilities for trajectory and topology operations, such as loading trajectories with atom selections, reducing frame counts, and detecting corrupted frames. MDTraj integration for trajectory merging and splitting is handled in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/mdt_spells.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/mdt_spells.py).

Robust error handling and system utilities are provided in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/auxiliar.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/auxiliar.py). This module defines custom exception classes for specific workflow issues (e.g., input validation, remote service errors) and includes functions for file I/O (JSON, YAML, binary data, downloads), string manipulation, and system processes. It also manages HTTP requests with retry mechanisms and timeout functionalities.

For ensuring reproducible computations, [`get_cksum_id`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/arg_cksum.py#L17) in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/arg_cksum.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/arg_cksum.py) generates a reproducible identifier for various Python data types. This allows for consistent comparison of values across different runs without storing the entire data, which is useful for caching and verifying computation integrity.

Interaction with remote MDDB servers is handled by the [`Database`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py#L240) and [`Remote`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py#L50) classes in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py). These classes manage retrieving node information, handling remote project data, and downloading various project files such as topology, structure, trajectory, input configurations, and analysis data. They also provide mechanisms for fetching reference data, handling aliases, and ensuring server reachability. The [`Remote`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py#L50) class specifically focuses on operations related to a particular project, providing access to project metadata and facilitating file downloads with progress reporting and robust error handling.

Additional utilities include atom selection management in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/selections.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/selections.py), which provides a [`Selection`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/selections.py#L6) class to handle collections of atom indices and convert selections for various external tools. File format detection and compatibility are addressed in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/formats.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/formats.py), which helps identify suitable functions or combinations of functions for different input and output format requirements. Filtering atoms from molecular structure and trajectory files based on selection strings is orchestrated by [`filter_atoms`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/filters.py#L26) in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/filters.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/filters.py), which handles input validation, auxiliary PDB generation, and dynamic selection of filtering functions.

The workflow also includes specialized analytical utilities. The [`BiBiTransformer`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/bibitransformer_nassa.py#L6) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/bibitransformer_nassa.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/bibitransformer_nassa.py) analyzes data distributions for binormality and bimodality using Gaussian Mixture Models, Bayes Factor, and Helguero's theorem. Nucleic acid sequence operations and configuration generation for NASSA are managed by [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/nucleicacid.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/nucleicacid.py) and [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/nassa_file.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/nassa_file.py), respectively, with visualization tools for heatmaps in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/heatmaps_nassa.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/heatmaps_nassa.py). BLAST operations against the Swiss-Prot database, including local database management and remote querying, are handled by [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/blast.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/blast.py). The [`Loader`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/loader.py#L42) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/loader.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/loader.py) interfaces with a NodeJS-based MDDB loader, managing configuration, SSH connections, and data loading. Finally, [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/httpsf.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/httpsf.py) provides a FUSE virtual filesystem for accessing single remote HTTP(S) files as if they were local, and [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/rich.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/rich.py) integrates Pandas DataFrames with the [`rich`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L52) library for improved terminal display. The [`Register`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/register.py#L11) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/register.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/register.py) tracks workflow execution history, warnings, and metadata.

## Molecular Dynamics Analysis Tools
The [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) repository provides a suite of analytical capabilities for processing molecular dynamics trajectories, contained primarily within the [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses) directory. This suite allows for detailed characterization of molecular systems, covering various aspects from membrane properties to conformational dynamics and interaction energies.

For analyzing membrane systems, the workflow includes tools to calculate the area per lipid (APL) using [`fatslim_apl`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/area_per_lipid.py#L1), which quantifies the average surface area occupied by each lipid molecule in a bilayer. Channel analysis, utilizing the [`CHAP`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/channels.py#L15) tool, identifies and characterizes pores or channels within proteins or membranes. Both analyses save processed data to JSON files and offer plotting functionalities. Lipid order parameters (S) are calculated using the [`gorder`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/lipid_order.py#L11) library for coarse-grained and united-atom simulations, or by direct C-H bond analysis for all-atom systems, providing insights into membrane fluidity and lipid acyl chain ordering. See [Specialized Biophysical Analyses](#molecular-dynamics-analysis-tools-specialized-biophysical-analyses) for a more detailed discussion.

Conformational dynamics are explored through several methods. Clustering analysis groups similar molecular snapshots based on RMSD, identifying representative conformations and transitions between them. This helps in understanding the major structural states visited during a simulation. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is applied to trajectories to identify the dominant modes of motion, both for overall structural changes and for changes in inter-residue contacts. Additionally, the workflow can generate data essential for constructing Markov State Models, which describe the kinetics and pathways of conformational transitions. For a deeper dive into these methods, refer to [Conformational Sampling and Dynamics Analyses](#molecular-dynamics-analysis-tools-conformational-sampling-and-dynamics-analyses).

The analysis of molecular interactions is also comprehensively covered. This includes the calculation of inter-residue distances, providing insights into proximity and binding events between different molecular components. Hydrogen bond analysis identifies and quantifies hydrogen bonding patterns, crucial for understanding molecular recognition and stability. Interaction energies, both electrostatic and Van der Waals, are computed using tools like [`CMIP`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L14) to evaluate the strength and nature of forces between specified molecular agents. Furthermore, specialized lipid interaction analysis classifies contacts by lipid type and their head/tail parts, elucidating specific binding preferences. More information on these interaction analyses can be found in [Intermolecular and Intramolecular Interaction Analyses](#molecular-dynamics-analysis-tools-intermolecular-and-intramolecular-interaction-analyses).

Beyond these, the suite also offers tools for assessing structural integrity through RMSD checks to detect sudden, unphysical jumps in trajectories, and for detecting and characterizing protein pockets using [`MDpocket`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/pockets.py#L6). These utilities are discussed in [Structural Integrity and Pocket Detection](#molecular-dynamics-analysis-tools-structural-integrity-and-pocket-detection). All analyses consistently leverage molecular data libraries such as [`mdtraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L22), [`pytraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L10), and [`MDAnalysis`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L877) for efficient data handling and often rely on external command-line tools, with results typically serialized into JSON format for interoperability.

### Specialized Biophysical Analyses
The [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) provides tools for specialized biophysical analyses crucial for understanding molecular systems. For membrane systems, the [`area_per_lipid`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/area_per_lipid.py#L12) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/area_per_lipid.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/area_per_lipid.py) calculates and visualizes the Area Per Lipid (APL). This involves using the external [`fatslim_apl`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/area_per_lipid.py#L1) tool for core APL calculations and [`griddata`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/area_per_lipid.py#L5) for interpolating results onto a grid, which are then saved as JSON and plotted.

Channel analysis, which identifies and characterizes pores or channels within a membrane, is handled by the functions in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/channels.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/channels.py). This module integrates with the external [`CHAP`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/channels.py#L15) tool to perform detailed analysis, processing its JSON outputs and PDB files to extract information about pore-lining and pore-facing residues. The process often involves reducing the trajectory size using [`get_reduced_trajectory`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_reduced_trajectory.py#L39) from [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_reduced_trajectory.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_reduced_trajectory.py) for computational efficiency.

Lipid order parameters, indicating the orientation and packing of lipid acyl chains, are computed by the [`lipid_order`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/lipid_order.py#L14) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/lipid_order.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/lipid_order.py). This function differentiates between all-atom (AA), united-atom (UA), and coarse-grained (CG) simulations. For AA simulations, it directly calculates C-H bond angles relative to the membrane normal. For UA and CG simulations, it leverages the external [`gorder`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/lipid_order.py#L11) library to perform calculations, parsing its YAML output.

For nucleic acids, the [`helical_parameters`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/helical_parameters.py#L115) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/helical_parameters.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/helical_parameters.py) orchestrates the analysis of helical parameters and other related properties. This involves executing external tools like [`cpptraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/pyt_spells.py#L42) for hydrogen bond analysis and [`Curves+`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/helical_parameters.py#L147)/[`Canal`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/helical_parameters.py#L417) for detailed helical parameter calculations. The outputs from these tools are processed to derive stiffness, averages, standard deviations, and backbone torsion populations (e.g., sugar puckering, alpha-gamma, and BI/BII populations), with results aggregated and saved in JSON format.

### Conformational Sampling and Dynamics Analyses
Methods for characterizing conformational dynamics include clustering, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on both structures and contacts, and the generation of data for Markov State Models.

Clustering analysis, as implemented in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/clusters.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/clusters.py), identifies and characterizes conformational clusters and transitions within molecular dynamics trajectories. This analysis can summarize the overall structural states and specific interaction interfaces by generating representative snapshots and detailed cluster data. The process involves defining atom selections, potentially reducing the trajectory size for efficiency, and calculating RMSD matrices. An iterative clustering algorithm then groups frames based on RMSD cutoffs, dynamically adjusting parameters to achieve a desired number of clusters. This analysis also identifies transitions between clusters and selects the "most representative frame" for each cluster for visualization.

Two distinct approaches are available for generating Markov State Model (MSM) data. The module [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/markov.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/markov.py) focuses on identifying the most populated frames within a trajectory, calculating the RMSD matrix between these frames, and generating corresponding visual representations. It efficiently extracts coordinates for high-population frames and computes RMSD values using selected atoms. Another module, [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/markov_2.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/markov_2.py), also identifies highly populated frames but constructs a transition probability matrix specifically among these selected frames. It takes pre-calculated population and transition data as input, filtering to a subset of key frames and their associated transition probabilities, along with generating screenshots of these frames. Both approaches prioritize memory efficiency by iteratively loading trajectory frames.

Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is applied to molecular dynamics trajectories through [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/pca.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/pca.py). This analysis generates PCA projections, eigenvalues, and projection data to describe the dominant modes of motion. The process involves parsing atom selections for fitting and analysis, potentially reducing the trajectory, and superimposing frames to remove translational and rotational motion. After applying PCA, the analysis extracts eigenvalues and eigenvectors, generating "projection" trajectories along significant principal components. Another PCA variant, found in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/pca_contacts.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/pca_contacts.py), focuses on inter-residue contacts. This tool computes distances between specified residue pairs, filters for frequently contacting pairs, and then applies PCA to smoothed contact distances. This identifies the principal components of contact variation, providing insight into how interaction networks evolve. The contact analysis can utilize either Pytraj or MDTraj libraries for trajectory processing and incorporates a sigmoid function to smooth distances before PCA, transforming them into a measure of contact strength.

### Intermolecular and Intramolecular Interaction Analyses
This section describes the analysis of various interactions within molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, including inter-residue distances, hydrogen bonding, and detailed interaction energies between agents.

Inter-residue distance analysis is handled by the [`distance_per_residue`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/distance_per_residue.py#L22) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/distance_per_residue.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/distance_per_residue.py). This function quantifies the spatial proximity between pairs of residues belonging to different interacting agents. It leverages [`pytraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L10) to efficiently calculate pairwise distances across the trajectory, computing both mean and standard deviation. To manage large datasets, it employs a reduction strategy where, if the number of calculated distances exceeds a predefined limit, the analysis is constrained to interface residues only. The results, including statistical summaries, are stored in JSON format for easy downstream processing.

Hydrogen bond analysis is performed by the [`hydrogen_bonds`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/hydrogen_bonds.py#L26) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/hydrogen_bonds.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/hydrogen_bonds.py). This module identifies and quantifies hydrogen bonds formed between specified molecular interfaces over the course of an MD simulation. It utilizes [`pytraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L10)'s hydrogen bond calculation capabilities to detect these interactions and then processes the results to focus on inter-agent hydrogen bonds, excluding those occurring within the same agent. The analysis accounts for [`pytraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L10)'s residue numbering schemes and can optionally incorporate population weighting and time-dependent analysis. To mitigate storage issues for extensive trajectories, the analysis typically focuses on a subset of frames.

Interaction energy calculations are conducted by the [`energies`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/energies.py#L45) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/energies.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/energies.py). This function uses the [`CMIP`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L14) (Classical Molecular Interaction Potential) tool to determine electrostatic and Van der Waals interaction energies between specified agents. The process involves preparing [`CMIP`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L14)-specific PDB input files that include atomic charges and "dummy" atoms (representing regions with low dielectric or atoms involved in strong bonds to prevent energy spikes). It dynamically adapts [`CMIP`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L14)'s grid parameters to ensure accurate and memory-efficient calculations, even for large systems, by preventing [`CMIP`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L14) failures related to atom limits or grid point limits. The function iterates through trajectory frames, extracts per-atom energies from [`CMIP`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L14) output, and then averages these energies over the entire trajectory, providing initial and final frame averages for various energy components. A debugging mode is available to generate [`CMIP`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L14) command lines for manual inspection.

Dihedral energy calculations are carried out by [`compute_dihedral_energies`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/dihedral_energies.py#L10) in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/dihedral_energies.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/dihedral_energies.py). This function computes torsion, electrostatic (EE), and Van der Waals (VDW) energies for specified dihedrals along an MD trajectory. It can reduce the trajectory size for performance and memory management. The calculations involve summing the energy of individual torsion terms and using Coulombic and Lennard-Jones potentials for EE and VDW energies, respectively. The averaged dihedral energies are saved in a JSON file.

Finally, lipid-protein interactions are analyzed by the [`lipid_interactions`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/lipid_interactions.py#L12) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/lipid_interactions.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/lipid_interactions.py). This module classifies and quantifies contacts between lipid molecules (categorized by head and tail parts) and protein residues. It supports atomistic, united-atom, and coarse-grained representations by dynamically selecting the appropriate analysis method. The process involves parallel computation across trajectory frames to detect contacts within a specified distance, accumulating contact events, and normalizing them by the total number of frames to derive interaction probabilities. The results are stored in JSON format and can be visualized. For a broader overview of analysis capabilities, refer to the [Comprehensive MD Analysis Suite](#md-simulation-data-lifecycle-and-analysis-comprehensive-md-analysis-suite).

### Structural Integrity and Pocket Detection
Tools for verifying the structural integrity of molecular dynamics trajectories, and methods for detecting and characterizing protein pockets, are provided within the workflow.

The structural integrity of trajectories is checked by detecting sudden Root Mean Square Deviation (RMSD) jumps between consecutive frames, which can indicate simulation artifacts or instability. This process, implemented in [`check_trajectory_integrity`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/rmsd_check.py#L29) within [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/rmsd_check.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/rmsd_check.py), calculates RMSD for entire molecular fragments or on a per-residue basis to identify outliers. The detection relies on z-scores of RMSD jumps; values exceeding a [`standard_deviations_cutoff`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L1222) are flagged. This analysis considers user-defined selections for atomic groups and applies a fragment-based approach to localize issues, preventing small localized jumps from being masked by overall stability. A more granular, per-residue RMSD jump analysis is also available, leveraging [`pytraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L10) for calculations.

Protein pocket detection and characterization are handled by the [`pockets`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/pockets.py#L45) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/pockets.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/pockets.py). This analysis utilizes [`MDpocket`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/pockets.py#L6) to identify and characterize druggable pockets from molecular dynamics trajectories. The process involves reducing the trajectory to a manageable number of frames, running [`MDpocket`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/pockets.py#L6) to generate a frequency grid of pocket occurrences, and then identifying and clustering these regions based on connectivity. For each significant pocket, [`MDpocket`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/analyses/pockets.py#L6) is re-run to extract dynamic data such as pocket volumes and implicated atoms. The results are then stored in a JSON file for further analysis.

## Project and MD Dataset Management
The system manages both projects and their individual Molecular Dynamics (MD) replicas through a centralized SQLite database. This database, defined within [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core), tracks the status of each project and MD, including whether it is new, running, or completed. It also stores relevant metadata and messages. A robust distributed filesystem locking mechanism ensures data integrity, preventing conflicts when multiple processes interact with the database, particularly across networked file systems.

The core of this management is handled by the [`Dataset`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L154) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py). This class is responsible for adding new projects and MDs to the database, querying their statuses, and updating their states as the workflow progresses. Projects and MDs are uniquely identified by UUIDs, allowing for flexible management even if their directory paths change. The system automatically refreshes the status of running jobs by checking active processes or SLURM job queues, marking them as [`ERROR`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L38) if they are no longer active. This ensures the database accurately reflects the current state of all ongoing simulations.

Beyond status tracking, the system facilitates the generation of configuration files, specifically [`inputs.yaml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/conftest.py#L90), using Jinja2 templates and Python generator functions. This allows for standardized and reproducible project setups. The [`Dataset`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L154) class also orchestrates the launching of commands and SLURM job scripts for filtered projects, supporting both sequential and parallel execution.

Input configuration for projects is managed and validated through the [`ProjectInputs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py#L36) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py). This class handles the loading and merging of input values from various sources, including file-based configurations and command-line overrides. It applies a clear precedence order, ensuring that explicit user inputs take precedence over file configurations, which in turn override default values. Input validation is performed against Pydantic schemas defined in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs_schema.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs_schema.py), which offers robust, field-specific checks while allowing for forward compatibility with unknown fields. This ensures that all project and MD-specific input parameters are correctly formatted and semantically valid before execution. The [`ProjectInputs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py#L36) class also includes sophisticated logic for merging MD-specific configurations, including the resolution of glob patterns for input directories and the validation of unique MD names and directories. This comprehensive approach to data management and input validation is central to maintaining the consistency and reliability of MD simulation projects.

### Project and MD Dataset Persistence and Status Tracking
The [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) system uses an SQLite database to manage the lifecycle and status of molecular dynamics (MD) simulation projects and their individual replicas. This database serves as a central registry for all projects and their associated MD runs, tracking their state from initial creation through execution to completion or error.

Project and MD entries are uniquely identified within the database by a Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) and their relative path ([`rel_path`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L2510)), allowing the system to track them even if their directory locations change. Each entry maintains a [`State`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L33) (e.g., [`NEW`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L35), [`WAITING`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L36), [`RUNNING`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L37), [`ERROR`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L38), [`DONE`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L39)), a descriptive message, and execution identifiers such as [`process_id`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L156) or [`slurm_job_id`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L156) when running.

The database schema, defined and managed by the [`Dataset`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L154) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py), includes [`projects`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/logger_and_loader.py#L12) and [`mds`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L1744) tables. The [`mds`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L1744) table, which stores individual MD replicas, is linked to the [`projects`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/logger_and_loader.py#L12) table via a foreign key with an [`ON DELETE CASCADE`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L176) constraint. This ensures that when a project is removed, all its associated MD replicas are automatically deleted from the database, maintaining data integrity. Furthermore, SQLite triggers are employed to automatically update the [`num_mds`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/console.py#L382) count in the [`projects`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/logger_and_loader.py#L12) table whenever MD entries are added or removed, preventing discrepancies.

A critical aspect of data integrity, especially in distributed computing environments, is the system's ability to refresh the status of [`RUNNING`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L37) entries. Before any data retrieval or display, the system actively checks if processes or SLURM jobs associated with [`RUNNING`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L37) entries are still active. If a process has terminated or a SLURM job is no longer in the queue, the system automatically updates the entry's state to [`ERROR`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L38), providing an accurate reflection of the workflow's progress. This proactive status refresh mechanism ensures that the dataset consistently presents reliable information about the ongoing simulations. More details on the concurrency control mechanisms can be found in [Distributed Filesystem Locking for Concurrency](#project-and-md-dataset-management-distributed-filesystem-locking-for-concurrency).

### Distributed Filesystem Locking for Concurrency
The [`DatabaseLock`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L42) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py) provides a mechanism to ensure data integrity and prevent race conditions when multiple processes attempt to access and modify the shared SQLite database. This is particularly important in distributed computing environments where standard file locking mechanisms might not function reliably across networked file systems. The approach leverages the atomic nature of directory creation to establish an exclusive lock.

A process can acquire a lock using the [`acquire`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L80) method, which attempts to create a unique directory as a lock file. This method incorporates a timeout to prevent indefinite waiting. Once operations requiring exclusive access are complete, the lock is released via the [`release`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L102) method, which removes the created directory. For streamlined usage, the [`lock_file`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L145) context manager simplifies the process of acquiring and releasing locks, guaranteeing that the lock is properly released even if errors occur during the protected operation. This distributed locking strategy is critical for maintaining consistency within the project and MD dataset, as detailed in [Project and MD Dataset Persistence and Status Tracking](#project-and-md-dataset-management-project-and-md-dataset-persistence-and-status-tracking).

### Advanced Input Configuration Resolution and Validation
The system manages and validates project input configurations through a sophisticated process that ensures data integrity and consistency across various sources. This is primarily handled by the [`ProjectInputs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py#L36) class, which is responsible for loading, merging, and resolving input values, supporting both declarative file-based configurations and dynamic command-line overrides.

Project input configurations are defined using Pydantic schemas, specified in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs_schema.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs_schema.py). These schemas provide robust validation for various aspects of the workflow, including ligand definitions, interaction parameters, and simulation metadata. For example, the [`Ligand`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs_schema.py#L35) schema includes validators to expand shorthand notations for PubChem IDs and ensure that at least one database accession is provided. The [`WorkflowInputs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs_schema.py#L122) schema, which is the main schema for the entire input file, incorporates field validators for specific parameters like [`orientation`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs_schema.py#L167), [`framestep`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs_schema.py#L149), and [`pdb_ids`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L2212), ensuring they conform to expected formats and constraints. This schema-driven validation helps to catch malformed inputs early in the workflow, preventing errors downstream.

The [`ProjectInputs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py#L36) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py) orchestrates the input process, beginning with the lazy loading and validation of the project's input document from a file (e.g., [`inputs.yaml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/conftest.py#L90) or [`inputs.json`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/constants.py#L67)). It supports [`$DIR`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/unittests/test_project_inputs.py#L23) replacements to enable relative pathing within the input files and includes legacy fixes for deprecated fields to maintain backward compatibility. Command-line [`forced_inputs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L1372) are normalized and applied, taking precedence over file-based inputs. When retrieving an input value, the system follows a clear precedence order: command-line overrides first, then values from the input file, followed by any explicit defaults provided, and finally, workflow-defined default values.

A key aspect of this input management is handling Molecular Dynamics (MD) specific configurations. The [`merge_md_config`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py#L195) method within [`ProjectInputs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py#L36) is designed to process MD configurations from various sources, including command-line arguments and glob patterns, allowing for flexible specification of multiple MD replicas. This method ensures that MD configurations are correctly merged and can be distinguished by whether they are topology or structure-based, according to supported formats. The [`validate_md_config`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/inputs.py#L309) method further ensures the uniqueness of MD configurations by autofilling missing names or directories and raising an [`InputError`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/auxiliar.py#L45) if duplicate entries are detected after autofilling, thereby maintaining data integrity for MD-specific parameters.

The system also provides mechanisms for persisting changes back to the input file, allowing for dynamic updates and autofilling of generated values. Input files can be checked for availability and, if necessary, generated from templates. This comprehensive approach to input configuration, validation, and resolution ensures that the workflow operates with well-defined and consistent parameters. For more details on how these validated inputs are then used to manage project and MD datasets, refer to [Project and MD Dataset Persistence and Status Tracking](#project-and-md-dataset-management-project-and-md-dataset-persistence-and-status-tracking).

## Workflow Utilities and Data Processing
The [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) repository includes a collection of tools and utilities that support the core molecular dynamics workflow, facilitating tasks from initial system characterization to data analysis and integration with external systems. This includes functionalities for counting atoms, analyzing protein chains through methods like InterProScan and UniProt mapping, validating input files, performing format conversions, filtering atoms, managing GROMACS mass definitions, and generating metadata. General utilities such as persistent caching, file operations, interaction with remote databases, BLAST searches, and wrappers for GROMACS and MDAnalysis are also provided.

For molecular system characterization and preprocessing, tools are available to accurately count atoms and residues, determine simulation box dimensions, and validate input files for common issues such as NetCDF corruption or GROMACS-specific mass definition problems. Specifically, [`fix_gromacs_masses`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/fix_gromacs_masses.py#L27) ensures that GROMACS uses a custom atom mass file that can be extended with new mass definitions, which is important for handling non-standard residues and ensuring GROMACS compatibility.

The system offers advanced protein and nucleic acid analysis capabilities. This includes mapping protein sequences to UniProt reference sequences, identifying protein domains using InterProScan, and integrating PDB data. The [`ProteinMapper`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_map.py#L104) class, defined in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_map.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_map.py), plays a central role in aligning protein chains from a structure to UniProt references, prioritizing various sources like forced inputs, local files, remote projects, PDB IDs, and BLAST searches to find the best match. This allows for detailed characterization of protein components, including specific features such as SARS-CoV-2 variant identification. Additionally, [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/chains.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/chains.py) handles the retrieval and processing of protein chain data, focusing on obtaining InterProScan analysis results for unique protein sequences, including job submission, status checking, and result fetching from the EBI InterProScan web service.

Cheminformatics and ligand identification are supported through tools that characterize non-standard residues and ligands within molecular systems. This involves generating InChIKeys, searching PubChem, and integrating with specialized databases like SwissLipids and LIPID MAPS.

Trajectory and structure transformation utilities allow for manipulation of molecular data. This includes converting between various file formats, efficiently extracting specific frames or reduced trajectories, and generating GROMACS-compatible topologies. The [`convert`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/conversions.py#L34) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/conversions.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/conversions.py) orchestrates these operations, dynamically selecting appropriate conversion functions based on input and output formats, and handling complexities like merging multiple trajectories or ensuring chain consistency during PSF to PDB conversions. Atom filtering is handled by [`filter_atoms`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/filters.py#L26), which filters atoms from simulation files based on selection criteria, ensuring consistency across filtered outputs.

Metadata generation is crucial for project management. [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py) creates comprehensive metadata for molecular dynamics projects and individual simulations, consolidating system properties, structural features, and simulation parameters into structured JSON files. This includes data from box size calculations, atom and residue counts, system keywords, reference mappings, and sequence metadata.

The utility set also includes persistent caching mechanisms, implemented in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/cache.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/cache.py), for optimizing workflow performance by storing and retrieving results of computationally expensive functions based on input checksums. File and path management, robust error handling, reproducible argument checksums via [`get_cksum_id`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/arg_cksum.py#L17), and managed interaction with remote MDDB databases via the [`Database`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py#L240) class are also core components.

Integration with external tools is achieved through specialized wrappers for GROMACS ([`run_gromacs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py#L22)), MDAnalysis ([`to_MDAnalysis_topology`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/mda_spells.py#L28)), Pytraj ([`get_pytraj_trajectory`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/pyt_spells.py#L16)), and MDTraj ([`merge_and_convert_trajectories`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py#L200)). These wrappers provide standardized interfaces for common tasks such as trajectory processing, atom filtering, and selection management, allowing the workflow to leverage the strengths of these specialized libraries while maintaining a consistent internal interface. For instance, [`run_gromacs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py#L22) provides an interface for executing GROMACS commands, handling environment variables, mass definition fixes, and output parsing. The [`Selection`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/selections.py#L6) class from [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/selections.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/selections.py) manages atom indices and converts them to formats compatible with various external tools like MDAnalysis, Pytraj, NGL, and VMD.

Finally, specialized analysis tools include the [`BiBiTransformer`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/bibitransformer_nassa.py#L6) class which analyzes data distributions for bi-normality and bi-modality, and the [`Register`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/register.py#L11) class which tracks workflow execution history, captures warnings, and stores workflow metadata, ensuring accountability and reproducibility.

### Molecular System Characterization and Pre-processing
The initial setup of a molecular dynamics project involves precisely characterizing the molecular system, which includes counting atoms and residues, determining simulation box dimensions, and validating input files. This process ensures the structural integrity and consistency of the starting configurations for simulations.

For atomic and residue-level characterization, the system counts various atom and residue types within a molecular structure, including proteins, nucleic acids (DNA, RNA), lipids, carbohydrates, solvent molecules, and ions. This detailed quantification helps in understanding the composition of the simulated environment. Atom counting functions within [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/atom_counters.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/atom_counters.py) use multiple libraries like [`mdtraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L22), [`pytraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L10), [`MDAnalysis`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L877), [`GROMACS`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docs/source/input.rst#L93), and [`VMD`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L10) to support various file formats and detect inconsistencies between topology, structure, and trajectory files. Specifically, [`get_atom_counts`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_atom_counts.py#L2) in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_atom_counts.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_atom_counts.py) categorizes and counts atoms and residues within a [`Structure`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/structures.py#L1197) object.

The dimensions of the simulation box are extracted from GROMACS topology and trajectory files. The [`get_box_size`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_box_size.py#L19) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_box_size.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_box_size.py) executes GROMACS commands to analyze these files and parse the output to determine the x, y, and z dimensions of the simulation box.

Rigorous validation of input files is crucial to prevent simulation errors. The system checks input structure, trajectory, and topology files for format consistency, NetCDF corruption, and atom count coherence. It includes mechanisms to detect and potentially fix issues like malformed PSF topology headers and atom count mismatches between topology and trajectory files. For instance, [`check_input_files`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/check_inputs.py#L29) in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/check_inputs.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/check_inputs.py) validates inputs and can correct PSF files by inserting empty lines where necessary to ensure compatibility with analysis tools. If atom count mismatches are detected where the topology has more atoms than the trajectory, the system attempts to filter the topology to match the trajectory's atom count. Furthermore, [`fix_gromacs_masses`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/fix_gromacs_masses.py#L27) in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/fix_gromacs_masses.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/fix_gromacs_masses.py) ensures that GROMACS uses a custom atom mass definition file, which can be extended to include specific or non-standard atom mass definitions, addressing potential issues with GROMACS's default settings and case sensitivity.

### Advanced Protein and Nucleic Acid Analysis
The system provides a suite of tools for the comprehensive analysis of protein chains and nucleic acids within molecular systems. This includes capabilities for mapping protein sequences to external biological databases, integrating structural data from the Protein Data Bank (PDB), performing domain identification, and calculating metrics related to system coverage and residue presence.

A central component for protein analysis is the [`ProteinMapper`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_map.py#L104) class, located in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_map.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_map.py). This class orchestrates the process of identifying protein chains within a molecular structure and mapping their sequences to UniProt reference sequences.
