It employs a prioritized approach, first checking for explicitly provided references, then local files, remote project data, and PDB-derived UniProt IDs. As a last resort, it utilizes a BLAST search ([`run_blastp`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/blast.py#L73)) to find potential UniProt matches for unassigned chains, ensuring that most protein sequences can be reliably characterized. The [`ProteinMapper`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_map.py#L104) also cleans protein sequences by replacing non-standard amino acid representations with 'X' to ensure robust alignment.

Once UniProt references are identified, the system fetches detailed information for each UniProt ID from the EBI UniProt API using [`get_uniprot_reference`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_map.py#L739) in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_map.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_map.py). This function retrieves essential metadata such as protein name, gene names, organism, sequence, and domain information, which is then structured for storage and further analysis. A specific algorithm is also integrated to identify SARS-CoV-2 variants in spike proteins by aligning sequences against a curated set of known COVID-19 spike variants, as detailed in [Curated SARS-CoV-2 Variant Sequences](#biological-resources-curated-sars-cov-2-variant-sequences).

The system further integrates with the EBI InterProScan web service for domain identification. The module [`prepare_chain_references`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/chains.py#L98) in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/chains.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/chains.py) handles the submission of unique protein sequences to InterProScan, monitors job status, and retrieves the results. This allows for the identification of conserved protein domains and functional sites. For additional details on this process, refer to [Comprehensive MD Analysis Suite](#md-simulation-data-lifecycle-and-analysis-comprehensive-md-analysis-suite).

For integrating structural data, the system retrieves and processes PDB entries from the RCSB PDB API. The [`prepare_pdb_references`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_pdb_references.py#L19) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_pdb_references.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_pdb_references.py) downloads PDB data, extracts relevant structural and biological information, and calculates Solvent Accessible Surface Area (SASA) for protein chains using GROMACS tools. It also establishes residue-level mappings between UniProt IDs and PDB chains, which is crucial for cross-referencing information between sequence and structural databases.

Finally, [`get_coverage_and_presence`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_coverage_and_presence.py#L11) in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_coverage_and_presence.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_coverage_and_presence.py) calculates the coverage and presence of protein and nucleic acid residues within the molecular system based on the established residue mappings and reference lengths. This provides a clear understanding of which parts of the biological references are represented in the simulation. The generated metadata, which includes all these characterizations, is consolidated using functions like [`prepare_project_metadata`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py#L14) and [`generate_md_metadata`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py#L294) in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_metadata.py), ensuring that each project and MD simulation is fully annotated with its protein and nucleic acid characteristics.

### Cheminformatics and Ligand Identification
The system provides capabilities for identifying and characterizing non-standard residues and ligands present within molecular systems. This includes generating unique identifiers for chemical compounds and integrating information from various external chemical and lipid databases.

The process of characterizing non-standard residues begins with generating InChI keys, which are standardized, non-proprietary identifiers for chemical substances. The [`generate_inchikeys`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_inchi_keys.py#L149) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_inchi_keys.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_inchi_keys.py) is responsible for creating these keys for non-standard residues found in a molecular structure. It leverages [`RDKit`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docs/source/tasks.rst#L20) for chemical structure analysis and handles specific molecular structures like ferroheme. These generated InChI keys serve as a basis for querying external chemical databases.

Ligand identification and characterization are handled by the [`generate_ligand_references`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_ligands.py#L90) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_ligands.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_ligands.py). This function identifies ligands by matching their InChI keys against the PubChem database, a public repository for chemical information. It supports various matching strategies, including similarity searches based on molecular descriptors. This functionality also integrates data from other specialized chemical databases like DrugBank and ChEMBL to provide a comprehensive characterization of identified ligands.

For lipid identification, the [`generate_lipid_references`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_lipids.py#L8) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_lipids.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_lipids.py) queries dedicated databases such as SwissLipids and LIPID MAPS. This allows the system to accurately classify and annotate lipid molecules within the simulation, augmenting the chemical information with lipid-specific details. This systematic approach ensures that all non-standard components, including various ligands and lipids, are identified, characterized, and their information is prepared for integration into the workflow.

### Trajectory and Structure Transformation Utilities
The [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) provides a suite of functionalities for manipulating molecular structures and trajectories, crucial for preparing and processing data within molecular dynamics simulations. These utilities handle various aspects, including format conversions, efficient extraction of specific frames or reduced trajectories, and the generation of comprehensive GROMACS-compatible topologies with detailed bond and charge information.

File format conversions are managed by the [`convert`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/conversions.py#L34) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/conversions.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/conversions.py). This function standardizes input file formats, merges multiple trajectories, and dynamically selects appropriate conversion routines based on the input and output formats. For instance, it can convert between various structure and trajectory file types and handles specific post-conversion checks, such as re-chaining [`Structure`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/structures.py#L1197) objects during [`psf`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/pyproject.toml#L72) to [`pdb`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L450) conversions to maintain consistent chain identifiers. This ensures that molecular data is available in the necessary formats for different simulation and analysis tools.

For efficient management of trajectory data, the workflow includes tools to extract specific frames or create reduced trajectories. The [`get_first_frame`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/mdt_spells.py#L267) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_first_frame.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_first_frame.py) extracts the initial frame of a trajectory, saving it as a PDB file. Similarly, functions like [`get_pdb_frames`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_pdb_frames.py#L12) in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_pdb_frames.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_pdb_frames.py) allow the extraction of selected frames or a subset of frames, which is particularly useful for analyses that don't require the full trajectory. To reduce computational load and storage, [`get_reduced_trajectory`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_reduced_trajectory.py#L39) in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_reduced_trajectory.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_reduced_trajectory.py) generates a shorter trajectory by calculating an optimal [`frame_step`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/pyt_spells.py#L80) and utilizing GROMACS [`trjconv`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py#L121).

A central component of the workflow is the generation of a standard topology file, which organizes molecular data for downstream analysis and database storage. The [`generate_topology`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py#L14) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/generate_topology.py) creates a comprehensive JSON topology file from a given molecular [`Structure`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/structures.py#L1197) object. This process includes:
*   **Atom Data Extraction**: Identifying and mapping unique atom species to optimize storage.
*   **Bond Representation**: Optimizing the representation of covalent bonds to minimize data size.
*   **Residue and Chain Data**: Extracting detailed information about residues and chains, including sparse storage for residue insertion codes.
*   **MD Charges**: Handling molecular dynamics charges, either by inlining them for small systems or storing them as binary files for larger systems to manage data size effectively.
*   **Selection Formatting**: Converting complex atom selections into an efficient, hierarchical format suitable for database queries.

Additionally, the system includes tools for extracting specific topological details such as bonds and charges. The [`find_safe_bonds`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_bonds.py#L270) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_bonds.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_bonds.py) extracts and validates molecular bonds from various sources like topology files or trajectories, even identifying "stable" bonds over multiple frames to avoid transient artifacts. It also handles exclusions for non-physical bonds, such as those involving coarse-grained atoms. Similarly, the [`get_charges`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L2152) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_charges.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/tools/get_charges.py) extracts atomic charges from different topology file formats, providing robust methods for handling various input types. These detailed topology components are essential for accurate simulation setup and subsequent analysis.

### Persistent Caching and General Utilities
The molecular dynamics workflow relies on robust utilities for optimizing performance through caching, managing file operations, handling errors gracefully, generating unique identifiers for reproducibility, and interacting with remote data sources.

A persistent caching mechanism is implemented by the [`Cache`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/cache.py#L8) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/cache.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/cache.py). This system stores and retrieves data from a specified file, with concurrency awareness to prevent data loss or corruption during simultaneous modifications. It employs an auxiliary file for atomic writes, ensuring data integrity. The cache can be refreshed to synchronize with external changes on disk, a crucial feature in environments with parallel processes. The [`get_cached_function`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/cache.py#L79) factory leverages this [`Cache`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/cache.py#L8) class to store and retrieve the results of arbitrary functions based on their input checksums, thus avoiding redundant computations.

Reproducibility and traceability are supported by the argument checksum generation provided by the [`get_cksum_id`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/arg_cksum.py#L17) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/arg_cksum.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/arg_cksum.py). This function generates a consistent identifier for various Python data types, including primitives, strings, exceptions, collections, and custom objects. For collections, it converts them to a JSON string or sorted list before calculating the checksum to ensure consistent ordering. For functions, it uses their bytecode and constants, providing a unique identifier for the function itself. This allows for reliable comparison of input values across different runs without storing the entire data.

General-purpose utility functions are encapsulated in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/auxiliar.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/auxiliar.py), providing a foundation for the workflow. This includes functionalities for file I/O (JSON, YAML, binary data, and downloads), string and data manipulation, and system-level operations. It also defines a set of custom exceptions to enable structured error reporting, allowing for quieter error handling for non-code-related issues. Network interactions are also handled, with robust HTTP request mechanisms that include retry logic with exponential backoff for network-related failures.

File and path management is handled by the [`File`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/file.py#L17) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/file.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/file.py). This class abstracts file paths and operations, normalizing paths and providing methods for checksum generation, existence checks, symlinking, copying, and renaming. It supports the identification of file formats based on extensions and handles [`pytraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L10) compatibility. An important feature is its ability to create symbolic links or, if symlinks are disallowed, perform file copies, enhancing flexibility across different file system environments.

Interaction with remote MDDB servers is facilitated by the [`Database`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py#L240) and [`Remote`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py#L50) classes in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py). These classes manage fetching project data, listing available files, and downloading various types of project-specific files, including topologies, structures, and trajectories. The [`Database`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py#L240) class resolves server aliases and checks server reachability, while the [`Remote`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py#L50) class handles specific project data. A custom [`workflow_urlopen`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/database.py#L30) function ensures consistent HTTP request headers and allows for conditional SSL certificate verification, which is useful in development or testing environments. For large file downloads like trajectories, a robust mechanism using temporary "incomplete" files ensures data integrity even if downloads are interrupted.

### Specialized MD Simulation Integration
Integration with molecular dynamics libraries and tools facilitates various tasks including trajectory processing, atom filtering, and selection management. The [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) provides wrappers for GROMACS, MDAnalysis, Pytraj, and MDTraj to enable this functionality.

The [`run_gromacs`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py#L22) function in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py) standardizes the execution of GROMACS commands, handling environment variable setup, mass definition issues, and output parsing. This includes functions for extracting structures ([`get_first_frame_structure`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py#L118)), merging and converting trajectories ([`merge_and_convert_trajectories`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py#L200)), and filtering atoms from various GROMACS-related files ([`filter_structure`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py#L291), [`filter_trajectory`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py#L323), [`filter_tpr`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py#L461)). These utilities streamline interactions with GROMACS by providing a consistent interface and automating common fixes.

The [`MDAnalysis`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L877) library is integrated through utilities in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/mda_spells.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/mda_spells.py) that create and manipulate [`Universe`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L877) and [`Topology`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/topologies.py#L21) objects. These functions enable the construction of [`MDAnalysis`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/mwf.py#L877) objects from custom JSON topology files, the setting of bonds and charges, and the identification and categorization of lipid molecules, including acyl chains and head/tail groups.

For Pytraj, the [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) provides utilities in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/pyt_spells.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/pyt_spells.py) for trajectory and topology operations. These include functions for loading trajectories with atom selections ([`get_pytraj_trajectory`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/pyt_spells.py#L16)), reducing the number of frames ([`get_reduced_pytraj_trajectory`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/pyt_spells.py#L62)), and creating new topology files based on [`Selection`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/selections.py#L6) objects ([`filter_topology`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/pyt_spells.py#L127)).

The management of MD trajectories using [`mdtraj`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/envs/environment.yml#L22) is handled by functions in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/mdt_spells.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/mdt_spells.py). These utilities support merging and converting trajectories ([`merge_and_convert_trajectories`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/gmx_spells.py#L200)), extracting subsets of trajectories ([`get_trajectory_subset`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/subsets.py#L14)), splitting merged trajectories based on RMSD jumps ([`split_merged_trajectories`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/mdt_spells.py#L299)), and reordering atoms within a trajectory ([`sort_trajectory_atoms`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/mdt_spells.py#L339)).

Atom selection across these different tools is unified by the [`Selection`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/selections.py#L6) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/selections.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/selections.py). This class manages collections of atom indices and provides methods for set operations (merge, subtract, intersection) and conversion to formats compatible with external tools like MDAnalysis, Pytraj, and GROMACS. This abstraction allows for consistent atom filtering regardless of the underlying molecular dynamics library used. More details on atom filtering can be found in [General Utilities and External Tool Integration](#md-simulation-data-lifecycle-and-analysis-general-utilities-and-external-tool-integration).

### Data Distribution Analysis and Workflow Register
Specialized tools are provided for analyzing data distributions and tracking workflow metadata. The [`BiBiTransformer`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/bibitransformer_nassa.py#L6) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/bibitransformer_nassa.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/bibitransformer_nassa.py) is designed to characterize data distributions by assessing binormality and bimodality. It fits both single-component and two-component Gaussian Mixture Models to input data, then compares them using Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) scores to determine if a distribution is uninormal, binormal, or if there is insufficient evidence to make a classification. For distributions identified as binormal, it further applies a modified Helguero's theorem to assess bimodality. This process aids in understanding the underlying nature of observed data distributions within molecular simulations.

The [`Register`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/register.py#L11) class in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/register.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/register.py) manages workflow execution history and metadata. It tracks the outcomes of tests, captures and deduplicates warnings, and stores relevant workflow metadata such as command-line arguments, execution time, date, and project version. The [`Register`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/register.py#L11) class persists its state to a JSON file, and upon initialization, it can load results from previous runs to maintain a continuous record of workflow activities. This functionality helps ensure reproducibility and provides a traceable history of operations and potential issues encountered during workflow execution.

## Manual Tools for Workflow Interaction
The [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools) directory contains scripts designed to facilitate direct interaction with the MDDB workflow. These tools bridge the gap between automated workflow execution and user-driven data management, configuration, and analysis.

One aspect involves querying and downloading project-specific data. The [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/api_tools.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/api_tools.py) script provides utilities for programmatic interaction with a REST API to retrieve project details, manage data, and download associated files such as [`topology.json`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docs/source/usage.rst#L116) directly from the database. This capability supports data integrity and consistent access within the MDDB ecosystem.

For structural manipulation, the [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/chainer.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/chainer.py) script automates the modification of PDB chain identifiers for specific atom selections. It interacts with [`VMD`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L10) (Visual Molecular Dynamics) to perform targeted changes and save the modified PDB files. This functionality supports the preparation or re-processing of structural data for MD simulations.

The directory also includes tools for generating workflow input configurations. The [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/inputs_generator_by_pdb.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/inputs_generator_by_pdb.py) script automates the batch creation of [`inputs.yaml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/conftest.py#L90) files, customizing each with a PDB ID derived from the directory name. The [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/inputs_generator.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/inputs_generator.py) script also exists for generating [`inputs.json`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/constants.py#L67) files that incorporate mutation and ligand details. These generators streamline the setup of new simulation projects by creating standardized configuration files.

Another utility is the [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/logger_and_loader.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/logger_and_loader.py) script, which processes project accessions to retrieve metadata, log project details, and initiate directory uploads. This tool automates the handling of new projects, fetching information from a database and coordinating the transfer of relevant data.

Finally, the [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/references_updater.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/references_updater.py) script systematically updates and generates various reference data—including proteins, ligands, PDBs, and chains—by querying external APIs and identifying orphan data. This ensures that the workflow operates with current and consistent reference datasets, supporting the accuracy of MD simulations and analyses. These manual tools provide mechanisms for interaction and data management within the MDDB workflow, supplementing its automated processes.

### REST API Utilities for Project Data Management
The [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/api_tools.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/api_tools.py) script provides tools for interacting with the MDDB REST API. It enables users to query project data, paginate through results, and download specific files associated with projects. The system manages the retrieval of project accessions and details through pagination, ensuring all relevant data is collected from the API. It also supports downloading various file types, such as configuration files, by constructing appropriate URLs and handling file storage. The default API endpoint used by these utilities is derived from the [`DEFAULT_API_URL`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/constants.py#L54) within the [`mddb_workflow.console`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/pyproject.toml#L25) module, specifically pointing to the [`/rest/current`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/logger_and_loader.py#L19) path. For an overview of other manual tools, refer to [Manual Tools for Workflow Interaction](#manual-tools-for-workflow-interaction).

### PDB Chain Modification using VMD
The [`chainer.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/chainer.py#L16) script, located at [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/chainer.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/chainer.py), facilitates the modification of PDB chain identifiers for specific atom selections within a PDB file. This is achieved through programmatic interaction with VMD (Visual Molecular Dynamics), an external molecular visualization and analysis program.

The script operates by dynamically generating a Tcl script that VMD then executes. This generated script contains commands to select a subset of atoms based on a user-defined selection string (following VMD's atom selection syntax) and to assign a new chain letter to these selected atoms. After the modification, VMD writes the updated PDB file to a specified output path. The script manages the lifecycle of this process, including creating the temporary VMD command script and subsequently removing it once VMD has completed its execution. This approach allows for automated, precise manipulation of PDB chain information without direct manual intervention within the VMD graphical interface.

### Automated Workflow Input Generation
The generation of workflow input files is facilitated by utilities that automate the creation of configuration necessary for molecular dynamics simulations. This process is crucial for streamlining the setup of new projects, especially when dealing with large datasets or complex experimental designs.

One approach involves the batch creation of [`inputs.yaml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/conftest.py#L90) files, which are derived from PDB structures. The script located at [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/inputs_generator_by_pdb.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/inputs_generator_by_pdb.py) reads a reference [`inputs.yaml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/conftest.py#L90) file and then generates customized [`inputs.yaml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/conftest.py#L90) files for multiple target directories. For each directory, the script extracts a PDB ID from the directory name, integrates this ID into the new configuration, and saves the customized [`inputs.yaml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/test/conftest.py#L90) file within that directory. This method ensures that each simulation run is correctly linked to its corresponding PDB structure.

Another utility, found at [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/inputs_generator.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/inputs_generator.py), focuses on generating [`inputs.json`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/utils/constants.py#L67) files that incorporate specific mutation and ligand details. While this script is noted as deprecated, it demonstrates a mechanism for populating workflow inputs with predefined ligand information and dynamically constructing descriptive names based on mutation and ligand parameters provided at the command line. This allows for the systematic configuration of simulations involving specific molecular modifications and interactions.

Both utilities serve to reduce manual effort and potential errors in preparing simulation input, contributing to the reproducibility and scalability of molecular dynamics projects.

### Project Accession Processing and Directory Uploads
The [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/logger_and_loader.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/logger_and_loader.py) script automates the retrieval of project metadata and the subsequent uploading of associated directories. It streamlines the process of managing project accessions by reading them from a [`pending.txt`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/logger_and_loader.py#L7) file. For each accession, it constructs a URL to query a database API, fetching critical project information. This metadata, particularly the project title, is then used to determine the local directory corresponding to the project. The script then orchestrates an external Node.js utility to handle the actual directory upload, passing both the generated directory name and the project accession. This external execution is crucial for abstracting the complexities of file transfer and ensuring proper resource management. The script integrates [`urllib.request.urlopen`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/api_tools.py#L18) for API interaction and [`subprocess.run`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/core/dataset.py#L311) to execute the external upload tool.

### Reference Data Updates and Management
The [`updater`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/references_updater.py#L32) function, located in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/references_updater.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/references_updater.py), automates the process of generating and updating various types of reference data, including proteins, ligands, PDB entries, and chains. This tool maintains up-to-date biological and structural information used throughout the MDDB workflow.

The core functionality of the script orchestrates the retrieval of project options from a configured database API and then fetches existing reference data. A key aspect of its design is the identification of "orphan" data; it distinguishes between project IDs that lack corresponding references and references that are no longer associated with any active projects. This mechanism helps ensure data consistency and prevents the accumulation of stale entries.

Based on the specified reference type (e.g., proteins, PDBs, chains), the [`updater`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/manual_tools/references_updater.py#L32) function invokes specialized sub-functions. For protein references, it retrieves fresh data from external sources and intelligently merges it with custom fields from older entries, preserving curated information. For chains, it interacts with external services like InterProScan, submitting sequences for analysis in batches and subsequently integrating the results. All processed and updated reference data are then saved into structured JSON files, making them readily accessible for other components of the workflow. This systematic approach ensures that the MDDB workflow operates with accurate and current reference information.

## Biological Resources
The [`mddb-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) repository includes a [`resources`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) directory for managing biological sequence data and processing scientific output files. This directory primarily serves two functions: providing curated biological sequence data, specifically for SARS-CoV-2 variants, and offering tools for processing and summarizing specific types of scientific output.

The module [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/resources/covid_variants.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/resources/covid_variants.py) contains a curated collection of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein amino acid sequences. These sequences, organized in a dictionary ([`covid_spike_variants`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/resources/covid_variants.py#L4)), allow for quick retrieval of specific variant sequences (e.g., Wild Type, Alpha, Delta, Omicron) for research and analysis purposes. This resource is valuable for studies requiring precise genetic information on different SARS-CoV-2 strains.

Another utility in this section, [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/resources/get_energies_sum.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/resources/get_energies_sum.py), processes output files from the CMIP tool. It extracts and aggregates energy components, specifically van der Waals and electrostatic energies, to provide a summarized view of interaction energies. This tool is designed to parse structured output, sum relevant energy values, and handle potential "infinity" values by filtering them out, thereby providing a numerical summary suitable for further analysis.

### Curated SARS-CoV-2 Variant Sequences
The [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/resources/covid_variants.py`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/resources/covid_variants.py) module provides a curated collection of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein amino acid sequences for various variants. This resource supports research and analysis within the workflow by offering a centralized repository for these sequences. The module defines a dictionary, [`covid_spike_variants`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/mddb_workflow/resources/covid_variants.py#L4), which maps common variant names (e.g., "WT", "Alpha", "Delta", "Omicron/BA.1") to their corresponding full spike protein amino acid sequences. This structure allows for direct and unambiguous retrieval of specific variant sequences. The sequences are manually curated, ensuring their reliability for downstream applications. This resource is part of the broader [Biological Resources](#biological-resources) section, which includes tools for processing scientific output data.

## Containerized Workflow Execution
The [`MDDB-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) is distributed as a Docker image, which encapsulates the entire runtime environment, including a Miniconda3 installation, all necessary dependencies, and the workflow software itself. This containerization ensures that the workflow executes consistently and reproducibly across diverse computing environments. The Docker build process, defined in [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile), creates a self-contained image ready for execution.

The Docker image builds upon a [`miniconda3:latest`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L2) base. It installs system-level dependencies like [`libgl1`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L10) to support graphical applications like VMD and then clones the [`MDDB-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) repository. A dedicated [`conda`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L41) environment, [`mwf_env`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L28), is created based on the [`environment.yml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L17) file within the repository, and the [`MDDB-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) Python package is installed into this environment. To ensure that the Python interpreter within the container can locate all necessary modules, the [`PYTHONPATH`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L31) is extended. An [`entrypoint.sh`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L34) script is generated and set as the container's entrypoint; this script uses [`conda run`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L41) to activate [`mwf_env`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L28) and execute any commands passed to the Docker container, thereby isolating the workflow's execution within its defined environment.

### Dockerfile Structure and Build Process
The [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile) defines the build process for creating a Docker image that encapsulates the [`MDDB-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) environment, ensuring consistent and reproducible execution across various computing environments.

The Docker build process begins by cloning the entire [`MDDB-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) repository into the image. Subsequently, a dedicated Miniconda3 environment, named [`mwf_env`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L28), is established within the container. This environment is configured based on the [`environment.yml`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L17) file located within the cloned repository, which specifies all necessary dependencies for the workflow. Following the environment setup, the [`MDDB-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) software itself is installed into this [`mwf_env`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L28) environment, enabling the execution of its components.

To facilitate seamless operation within the container, the [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile) also extends the [`PYTHONPATH`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L31) to ensure Python can correctly locate all [`MDDB-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) modules. A key aspect of the container's design is the generation of an [`entrypoint.sh`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L34) script. This script serves as the primary execution point for the Docker container, utilizing [`conda run`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L41) to activate the [`mwf_env`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L28) and execute workflow commands in a properly isolated environment. The [`entrypoint.sh`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L34) script is then set as the [`ENTRYPOINT`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L39) for the Docker image, dictating the command that will be executed when the container starts.

For a deeper understanding of how this entrypoint script functions during container execution, refer to [Entrypoint Script and Container Execution](#containerized-workflow-execution-entrypoint-script-and-container-execution).

### Entrypoint Script and Container Execution
The [`entrypoint.sh`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L34) script, generated as part of the Docker image build process, serves as the primary execution point for the containerized MDDB workflow. This script is dynamically created by the [`/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile) and is central to ensuring proper environment isolation and reproducibility within the container. It uses [`conda run`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L41) to activate the [`mwf_env`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L28) Conda environment, which contains all necessary dependencies and the installed [`MDDB-workflow`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/README.md#L4) software. By designating [`/app/entrypoint.sh`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L39) as the [`ENTRYPOINT`](https://github.com/mmb-irb/mddb-workflow/docker/Dockerfile#L39) for the Docker container, any command issued to the container will be executed within this controlled environment, guaranteeing that the workflow operates with its specified dependencies. This approach ensures consistent execution across various deployment environments. Further details on the Docker image construction can be found in [Dockerfile Structure and Build Process](#containerized-workflow-execution-dockerfile-structure-and-build-process).
